column15: No web presence found. Naming pattern ('Platinum', 'First West') gives no clear nationality signal, so left unclassified rather than guessed.
Barton 1792 Distillery, Bardstown KY; standard bourbon mashbill, no peat mentioned anywhere

Contrary to my first guess (a New Zealand independent bottler), 36southwhisky.com redirects straight to morrisofrutherglen.com/pages/36-south-whisky: 36 South is produced by Morris of Rutherglen in Victoria, Australia (name references 36 degrees south latitude), matching the catalogue's own AU guess. "36 South Double Grain Whisky" made from local wheat/barley; page's own tasting language ("smooth yet complex") has no smoke/peat descriptor -- no cask-finish/Morris-cask connection stated on that page despite the sample name.
John O'Groats, Caithness; first spirit run 2022, officially opened by King Charles III in Aug 2023. No peat statement found in the Wikipedia article.
North Wales single malt distillery (first in North Wales since the early 1900s). Official site does not explicitly say "unpeated", so confidence kept low despite no indication of peat use.

Confirmed by this project's own reference authority table (region=Lowland, owner=Morrison Scotch Whisky Distillers, malt, operating) -- matches the catalogue's own sample naming "Aberargie Morrison" directly. Official site (fetched this session) states only "balanced, elegant" character and first-fill bourbon/sherry cask maturation, with no explicit peat/unpeated statement, so peatProfile is left unknown rather than guessed.
Own-label style, no independent web presence found; treated as an ordinary unpeated blended Scotch per brief long-tail default, not brand-verified.
Standard unpeated sherried Speyside malt; extremely well-established, equivalent tier to Macallan/Glenfiddich.

Isle of Lewis distillery (aka Red River distillery), operating since 2008; earliest release was 'Spirit of Lewis' before the current Abhainn Dearg-branded single malts. No peat/smoke level stated in Wikipedia's product list or the distillery's own site (fetched, JS-rendered, no extractable peat claim).

Family-run distillery on Achill Island, Co. Mayo, founded 2015. Makes both an unpeated core and a distinct 'Peated' single malt (see rule), plus single pot still - range spans types so defaultTypeName left empty.

Independent bottler revived 1993 (original 1826 Glasgow distillery closed 1907); also owns Ardnamurchan distillery, not relevant here since this batch's samples ("Adelphi", "Adelphi Maclean's Nose") name no specific source distillery.

Confirmed single malt Scotch whisky brand of William Grant & Sons (listed alongside Glenfiddich/Balvenie/Kininvie/Ailsa Bay) but its specific source distillery is not disclosed/confirmed this session - parentSlug deliberately left empty. Peat left unknown since WG&S's Ailsa Bay site does produce a lightly-peated component for blending, so "none" cannot be assumed confidently.

Real Swedish distillery in Arboga (agitatordistillery.com, "Agitator ar ett svenskt destilleri i Arboga"). Could not confirm peat level of any expression, so left unknown (no citation opened to support none/light/medium/heavy - sourceUrls therefore left empty per the peatProfile=unknown rule). REVIEWER FLAG: "Agitator Rok" - "rok"/"rok" resembles Swedish "rok" (smoke); this sample may be a smoky/peated expression but I could not verify it, so no rule was written - worth a manual check.
No information found for this brand within budget (no Wikipedia coverage). Single sample 'Aikan Extra Collection Batch No.3' gives no clear indication of origin, distillery or type.

One of the very few peated Lowland distilleries; cited article: "Ailsa Bay and Annandale have become characterised by their use of peat, with a flavor profile more typical of Islay whisky." Exact ordinal is uncertain -- some releases are reported elsewhere as very lightly peated (~1.2ppm "Sweet Smoke"), others heavier for blending stock, so treat "medium" as approximate and verify against the specific expression actually in stock.

Official site (ei-sake.jp) describes the Akashi single malt's taste as '...medium, light, slightly peaty'; the Akashi blended whisky is described as smooth/dry with no peat mention. Legal distillery name is White Oak (Eigashima Shuzo); no separate White Oak catalogue entry in this batch so Akashi is modelled as the distillery-level row. defaultTypeName left empty: range spans single malt and blended.

Sample "Alchemist Tobermory" reads as an independent bottler's expression of Tobermory single malt; no citation confirms which "Alchemist" company this is (several drinks businesses use the name). countryCode GB-SCT is a low-confidence inference from bottling a Scotch distillery, not a confirmed fact. A tobermory distillery row is emitted below (required per BRIEF.md sec.2 regardless of this bottler's own identity) so the in-name distillery match can resolve.
Could not identify producer despite research; only Alexander Aqva Di Vita Amarone Cask Finish sample available. Possibly Italian or generic European. Flag for reviewer.
Wikipedia confirms Pernod Ricard/Chivas Brothers ownership and Speyside location. No distillery-specific peat statement; defaulted to unpeated per Speyside's general house style.

Japanese "World Blended Whisky" from Mars Whisky (Hombo Shuzo / Mars Shinshu distillery), released in numbered wood-finish editions (sherry cask, Mizunara, red wine, Yamazakura). Lookup attempts for this brand specifically returned no usable content this pass; peat left unknown rather than assumed.

Standard single malt is unpeated. See rule.tsv for Peated (medium, ~23-24ppm) and Fusion (light, 25% peated Scottish malt); Kadhambam/Portonova/Raj Igala are cask-finish variants of the standard unpeated malt, no rule needed

Known undisclosed/teaspoon brand for Highland Park, named explicitly as a sibling pair in this research task's own brief; peat level assumed identical to parent since it is reportedly the same liquid under another label.

Knockdhu distillery. Modern core range is unpeated (evolved from an originally peaty 1894 style); since 2014 a separate "Peaty Collection" (Cutter, Flaughter, Tushkar, Peatheart, Sherry Cask Finish Peated Edition) uses malt peated to ~20ppm - see rule row. Region recorded as Highland (Knock, Aberdeenshire, near the Speyside boundary); some sources place it in Speyside instead - low-confidence detail flagged for reviewer, though it does not affect the peat call.

Input brand string '& Whisky' does not correspond to any single identifiable producer - its 6 sample product names (Umiki, Kura The, Lord Moisans, Scottish Piper, MacKinlay's Old) look like several unrelated real brands (Japanese blends, MacKinlay's Scotch) rather than one house style. Likely a catalogue category/parsing artifact, not a real brand. Not researched as a single entity; alias emitted only for the exact catalogue string as required.

Louisville, Kentucky bourbon distillery known for port-cask finishing (its whole signature, not a separate 'Port Cask' sub-brand -- the two samples are both just the core product). Ownership (Bacardi Limited, acquired 2015) is from general knowledge; a dedicated Wikipedia fetch attempted this session 404'd on the title tried, so that specific fact is NOT independently re-verified -- only the general Whisky article backs the peat=none category claim.

Owns Glencadam and Tomintoul distilleries and also bottles blends (e.g. "Glen Parker") under its own name; treated as a bottler/owner-company since the catalogue brand spans multiple sub-brands. See glencadam row.

Distillery itself is never the bottling name: output is split into two differently-branded single-cask ranges, Man O' Words (unpeated, named for Robert Burns) and Man O' Sword (peated, named for Robert the Bruce) -- see those rows (parentSlug=annandale). peatProfile left unknown here since nothing is sold as plain 'Annandale'.

Own blended-Scotch brand of Tomatin Distillery Co (alongside Talisman). Tomatin's own house style is one of the least-peated Highland malts, so the blend is inferred unpeated; no source found stating this directly for Antiquary itself.

Source list marks this 'malt' but Wikipedia's Products section only documents Arbikie 1794 Highland Rye (Scotland's first commercial rye whisky in 100+ years) alongside gin/vodka -- no single malt is described -- so defaultTypeName left empty rather than forced to 'single malt' (range may span types / may not include a malt at all). No peat/smoke level stated anywhere fetched.
One of the most heavily peated Islay malts, roughly 50-55ppm. Owned by LVMH via The Glenmorangie Company since the 1997 reopening.

Original 1896 Ardgowan distillery in Greenock burned down in 1903 ('a river of flaming whisky'); modern distillery on Ardgowan Estate near Inverkip operating since 2016. No peat/smoke level found in the (history-focused) Wikipedia article.

'The only remaining Highland distillery to fully peat their standard malt.' Current OB Legacy is an 80% peated / 20% unpeated vatting. Historically the signature malt in Teacher's blend. Named in Artist series samples (this batch).
Islay's newest distillery (opened 2019), owned by Hunter Laing. Standard malt spec is 40ppm phenol, comparable to Port Charlotte's 40ppm (recorded heavy in this batch).

Confirmed the distillery makes BOTH peated and unpeated styles from the outset (cited source). Could not confirm whether the catalogue's sample "Ardnamurchan AD" batch code denotes the peated or unpeated style (or a marriage of both) - deliberately left unknown rather than guessed; worth a human check against the actual bottle/batch.
Founded by master blender Andrew Rankin from 2015, ~GBP50m project, planning approved 2017. No peat/smoke level or distinct brand name found.

French single malt, founded 2022, distilled at Distillerie Tessendier (Maison Boinaud) in Jarnac, Charente. Site lists a "Peated" expression (French: Tourbe) as a distinct product from "Original", implying the core/Original line is unpeated - see rule row for the peated "Tourbe" expression. Intensity of Tourbe not confirmed with ppm data.

First French single malt (launched 1998), made by the Warenghem Distillery in Brittany. No peat information confirmed either way this session. FOR REVIEWER: the 'Yeun Elez' expression (in my sample list) is named for a peat bog/moor in the Monts d'Arree, Brittany, by Breton place-name - it may well be a peated bottling distinct from the 'Classic' line, but I found no fetched source confirming this; worth checking before assuming the whole range is uniform.
Lochranza, est. 1995 by ex-Chivas Brothers MD Harold Currie. Unpeated core range (10yo, Bothy, Bodega). Peated sibling line is Machrie Moor (this batch, parentSlug=arran).

Numbered independent-bottler series by La Maison du Whisky (Paris), covering many distilleries worldwide incl. Karuizawa, Caol Ila, Macallan, Bowmore, Linkwood, Ardmore (all seen in samples). Peat varies per release; resolve via in-name distillery match.

French independent-bottler range from La Maison du Whisky; deliberately spans every Scotch region and style, peated and unpeated, so no house peat level. Samples name Ardmore (own row in this batch), Caol Ila, Ben Nevis, Glen Elgin, Glen Ord and Linkwood -- distillery rows added below per the independent-bottler rule.

Atom Brands (confirmed parent of That Boutique-y Whisky Company) - independent bottler. Samples name Macduff and Longmorn (Scotch malt distilleries, rows added), Heaven Hill (US bourbon distillery, row added), plus own "World Blend" and undisclosed "Atom Irish #1/#2".
Unpeated malt, triple-distilled -- signature Lowland style. Named in Old Malt Cask samples.
Wikipedia confirms Speyside/Diageo. No distillery-specific peat statement; defaulted per Speyside general house style.
Added to resolve Scyfion's sample bottlings. Cited page confirms region/owner but not peat explicitly; unpeated is standard for this Speyside malt.
No Wikipedia article or independent confirmation found this session. Flag for reviewer.
No information found this session; samples are 'Back to Black' / 'The Story of Back to Black' - own-label, origin unclear, not searched (long tail budget)

Catalogue spells it "BAGOTS" (Grain Game, Madeira Cask, Triple Batch, White Moscatel Cask -- cask-finish naming typical of small-batch/craft bottlings). No Wikipedia page or other citable source found; country and category could not be determined this session.

Part of Jim Beam's small-batch bourbon collection (alongside Knob Creek/Basil Hayden/Booker's), distilled at Jim Beam's Clermont/Boston, KY site. 'jim-beam' is an extremely well-known distillery slug another batch will almost certainly emit -- not created here.
Distilled from unpeated barley grain; historically a blending malt, bottled as vintage releases since 2007.

Fingerprint malts (Miltonduff, Glenburgie) are unpeated Speyside distilleries; wiki page describes the 21 Year Old as "spicy, aromatic and heather smoke", implying a light smoky character at least in aged expressions. Core Finest not separately described in the source, so confidence kept low rather than assuming it is identical to the 21yo.

A lime-infused, sweetened Scotch-based "spirit drink" (35% ABV, sugar + vanilla extract added) rather than a standard whisky - FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW of categorisation. Base Ballantine's blend is generally light/touch-of-smoke, but given the heavy flavouring/dilution here peat character is uncertain, left unknown rather than inherited
~55ppm heavily peated; produced at Edradour distillery since 2003, first release 2006. Sibling of unpeated Edradour, same distillery.

Formerly 'Connacht Distillery' (Co. Mayo, est. 2015), rebranded Ballina in 2025 after acquisition by Terroirs Distillers (Tullibardine's owner). First releases Dubailte (double wood) and Triarach (triple wood), 100% Irish malted barley. No peat/smoke mentioned in sources found.
Archived whisky.com page quotes distillery manager Colin Poppy: the intended style 'is not smoky, but strong and expressive'. Scotland's first single-estate distillery (own barley, own maturation).
Official site (fetched) carries only marketing copy ('Nothing Wasted, Nothing Rushed, Nothing Ordinary'); no peat/smoke claim, and no Wikipedia article exists yet. Very new, obscure operation.

Archived whisky.com: 'The whiskies of Balmenach are rather fruity and not peated, which is very typical for a Speyside distillery... The malt of the Balmenach distillery is always unpeated.' scotchwhisky.com confirms Inver House has no plans to release it as a single malt at all -- almost everything on the market is via independent bottlers (Gordon & MacPhail, Douglas Laing).

Core range (DoubleWood, PortWood, Montilla, 12/14/17/21) is unpeated. Distillery restarted an annual one-week peated malting run in 2001 ("Peat Week"); those limited releases (Peat Week, Peated Triple Cask, Week of Peat) are heavily peated - see rule rows.
Single-product entry; whiskybase.com confirms the brand exists in its database but no identifying detail (origin, style, country) was found. Long-tail, fast-tracked per budget rules.
Roughly 150-year-old recipe recreated in 2012 by A.D. Rattray: 40% Speyside/Highland malt with 60% Lowland grain. The base blend is unpeated; a separate "Peated Reserve" exists, see rule.

Blackpool, England distillery (est. 2019, Halewood-backed). Produces both peated and unpeated English malt spirit (EM/PEM/PBM plus corn/rye/wheated mashes); flagship "Distiller's Cut" is the bourbon-inspired, non-"Peated"-labelled single malt. See rule for explicitly "Peated"-labelled releases.
Own-label blended Scotch (not the bank), 2 products in this batch. No web presence found this session.

Non-distilling independent blender of American whiskey and rum, Louisville KY, founded 2013; sources casks from multiple distilleries so has no single house peat level. Samples (Vantage, Dovetail, Seagrass, Batch 036, Foundation, Rye Batch 004) name no source distilleries, so no distillery rows added
No information found. 'Honey' and 'Spisy' [sic, likely 'Spicy'] variants suggest a flavored whisky-based product; origin and type could not be determined within budget.

No web presence found this session (official domain unreachable, Wikipedia search returned nothing but Simpsons/Ireland false positives). Alias kept at any-scope only after judgement that "Bart's" (6 chars incl. apostrophe) is a reasonably distinctive token for a whisky catalogue -- flag for reviewer if this proves too permissive.

Lightest-bodied of the Jim Beam small-batch bourbon family, high-rye mashbill. defaultTypeName left empty: the line also includes a Dark Rye expression alongside the bourbon. parentSlug=jim-beam expected to be seeded by another batch (globally known Beam Suntory distillery/brand) -- not created here.

Product names repeat French-Revolution imagery ('1789', 'No.7 1789'), the basis for countryCode=FR; 'Daucourt' (in one sample) is confirmed on Wikipedia to be only a French surname, not a spirits company, so that lead was dropped rather than guessed at

Could not identify what this producer actually is. Samples ("Whiskey and Apple Juice", "Penicillin (Пеніцилін) 11 порцій") read as a flavoured/cocktail-kit product line (Penicillin is a well-known Scotch cocktail) rather than a conventional whisky brand; no dedicated Wikipedia article found. REVIEWER FLAG: this is a different entity from the "bayadera" store already in this codebase (a Ukrainian retailer) - no technical collision since producers and stores are separate tables, but worth a human sanity check on whether these SKUs belong in the whisky KB at all.

Possibly named for the Beara Peninsula, Co. Cork; no producer/distillery identified this session (official domain unreachable). defaultTypeName left empty: catalogue types the bare "Beara" sample as grain but its "Black Cask Blend" sibling as blend.
Triple Grain sample suggests a grain-whisky blend; country/origin not confidently identified (could be French) -- no search performed this pass.
Own-label / limited bottling ('Thunder in the Glens Anniversary'), no web presence found; fast-tracked per own-label rule.
No web presence found this session. The "Butterscotch Liquor" sample suggests a flavoured whiskey liqueur variant rather than a straight whiskey for that specific expression.

Mainstream Diageo blend (Arthur Bell & Sons, per general knowledge - dedicated Wikipedia page returned 404 this session). No distillery-specific peat statement found; defaulted to unpeated per ordinary-blend category norm. "Bell's Spiced" is a spiced/flavoured variant, not a peat indicator - no rule needed.

Official site (fetched) describes a small-batch triple-distilled single malt/single cask project near Dumfries; founders 'one Scottish, one Irish' drawing on 'Irish and Scottish whisky making traditions' (triple distillation is an Irish-style choice, but no explicit peated/unpeated statement was made). No Wikipedia article; the site's own target opening was 2023, current status unconfirmed.
Added to resolve Artist Collective's sample bottlings. Cited page confirms region/owner but not peat explicitly; unpeated is standard for this Highland malt.

First spirit flowed June 2024; first bottling not expected until 2029. Wikipedia (Times, 2024) says production uses 'local peat and heather... in the process' alongside bere barley, but does not say this is peated malt/kilning versus some other use of peat, and the intended profile is described only as 'classically maritime'. Left unknown rather than guessing an intensity from that one ambiguous phrase -- flagged for reviewer to re-check once the whisky is actually released.

Core range (The Original Ten/Twelve etc.) is unpeated. Distillery also bottles peated expressions under distinct line names within the BenRiach brand itself (Curiositas, Smoky Ten/Twelve, Birnie Moss, Septendecim, Authenticus) -- captured as rules below rather than sibling brands, since they are always sold as "BenRiach <name>", not a standalone brand name. Owner Brown-Forman inferred from the 2016 GlenDronach/BenRiach/Glenglassaugh group acquisition (corroborated on the Glenglassaugh distillery page), not independently opened for BenRiach itself.
Wikipedia does not explicitly state unpeated; inferred from no peat/smoke mention and its role as a Diageo blending malt

Core range is Speyside's classic lightly-peated house style (brief's own calibration example). Peat Smoke is a separate heavily-peated bottling in the distillery's own lineup, see rule (matches brief's own worked example verbatim).

Single product, no information found this session; 'Bercloux' is a commune name in Charente-Maritime, France, but not confirmed as this brand's actual origin so countryCode left empty rather than guessed

Bernheim Original, a straight wheat whiskey made by Heaven Hill at their (New) Bernheim distillery, Louisville. defaultTypeName left empty since "wheat whiskey" has no exact match in the closed type list. Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.

Historic London wine & spirits merchant and independent bottler (BBR range), est. 1698 - well-established general knowledge, but no page was opened for it this session, so left without sourceUrls and confidence dropped to low accordingly (peatProfile is correctly unknown for a bottler regardless). Sample "Berry Bros. Lochindaal 2010 Cask #4339" - "Lochindaal" could not be confirmed as a historical Bruichladdich brand name this session (the Bruichladdich Wikipedia article does not mention it), so no separate Lochindaal row was created; a reviewer familiar with Bruichladdich's older naming should check this.

No web presence found: Wikipedia search returned zero hits (only suggested 'Bieberbach'), and guessed official domains (beverbach.de/.com) failed to resolve/connect. Name suggests a German/European craft origin given the cask-finish naming (Tri Cask, Sherry Cask, Tequila Cask, Mizunara Cask, Craftbeer Cask) but this is entirely unconfirmed.
Sourced small-batch bourbon (6 Year). American bourbon mash bills do not use peated malt, but no source specific to this brand was opened, hence confidence=low.

Catalogue lists this same name 3 times with inconsistent country/type (DE/blend, US/rye, US/blend); countryCode=US taken as the majority value, not a confirmed fact. No producer identified this session.
Douglas Laing's blended malt of Islay single malts only (Ardbeg, Bowmore, Caol Ila, rare Port Ellen); part of the Remarkable Regional Malts range, heavily peated/smoky.

No producer identified this session (no useful search hits). peatProfile=none rests on the general bourbon-is-unpeated category convention, not a brand-specific source (matches this project's own batch-08 precedent for an equally unconfirmed US bourbon label).

2013 reformulation reduced Islay malt content to Bunnahabhain alone. scotchwhisky.com: master blender wanted to move away from the brand having "lost itself in Islay"; today's blend is described as "lightly to moderately smoky" with floral/oak/fruit/honey/nutmeg notes alongside the smoke.
Listed as "Blended Scotch Whisky" among Duncan Taylor's own brands. Core range (Black Bull, Kyloe, Kyloe Sherry Finish) unpeated; a separate "Peated" variant exists (see rule.tsv).

Budget blended Scotch label (incl. a 'Bourbon Finish' variant per sample); owner not confirmed this session. peatProfile rests on the general Highland/Speyside/Lowland-dominated blend character described on the Scotch whisky Wikipedia page (only Islay/Campbeltown are described there as peaty/smoky), not brand-specific evidence.

Canadian blended whisky, own distillery in Lethbridge AB; owned by Heaven Hill since 2019 (previously Constellation Brands). No explicit peat statement found; Canadian whisky has no peat tradition. defaultTypeName left empty - Canadian whisky has no clean match in the closed type list

No Wikipedia article and no resolvable official website found (two plausible domains failed DNS resolution). Extremely new/obscure Falkirk-area project; nothing fetchable to cite. Alias kept brand-scoped only: 'blackness' is an ordinary English word.
Lowland style is conventionally the least peated in Scotland; the Wikipedia article only documents historical (1887) peat-fired kilning, not a current spec, so confidence is low.
Unpeated malt; core component of the Bell's blend. Named in Old Malt Cask samples.

Blairfindy is a real historic place/castle name in the Glenlivet area of Speyside (Wikipedia's Glenlivet article surfaces it), likely used here as an independent single-cask label name rather than a distillery of its own -- region/legalRegion given from that toponymy alone (low confidence). Treated as an undisclosed-origin label per the brief's rule 3: producer and true source distillery not guessed.
First modern single-barrel bourbon brand (1984). Brand legally owned by Age International Inc; produced/marketed by Sazerac at Buffalo Trace Distillery.
'Pact' series -- master distiller John Rempe combines sourced/aged bourbons into limited annual vattings (a true blend, no single distillery of origin). Kentucky straight bourbon, no peat.

Single generic colour-word name; could not be identified as any specific brand and is below the 5-character alias floor regardless. Kept as a minimal row only so the (necessarily brand-scope) alias exists; note in alias.tsv that it will not resolve in-name.
Likely named after the Irish folk-song character "Bold Thady Quill"; no producer identified this session.

Wikipedia: the modern 'Bomberger's'-branded whiskey (e.g. 'Bomberger's Declaration' in my sample) is a Michter's product with 'no direct connection' to the historic 1753-1989 Bomberger's/Michter's Distillery site in Pennsylvania (a National Historic Landmark, now non-operating). parentSlug=michters is not a row in my own producer.tsv - Michter's is a well-known US whiskey brand/producer another batch will very likely cover; flag if it does not. peatProfile via the generic bourbon-category fact.

Believed (general knowledge, not confirmed this session) to be a Bladnoch-associated blended Scotch from an earlier ownership era; the current Bladnoch site does not list it and no other citation was found.

Edinburgh-area Lowland distillery; per Wikipedia (Aug 2025) the range now includes both a 47% ABV non-peated spirit and a 51% ABV peated spirit, both matured in Muscat casks, with no separate brand name splitting the two (contrast Annandale's separately-named Man O'Sword / Man O'Words). Left as a single unknown-peat row for that reason rather than guessing which release a catalogue listing means.

Believed to be Boone County Distilling Co. (Independence, Kentucky) from general knowledge - not verified via a fetched source this session, so the kind=distillery call is a judgment call, not a confirmed fact. peatProfile via the generic bourbon-category fact (charred-oak/corn-mash process, no peat-smoking step described anywhere for bourbon production), not brand-specific.

First Scotch distillery in the Scottish Borders since 1837 (Hawick, opened 2018); also makes William Kerrs Gin (unrelated to whisky naming). No peat/smoke level stated in the (fully read) Wikipedia article. Alias kept brand-scoped: 'Borders' is a common geographic word.

Colorado craft distillery; its own site states "American Single Malt Whiskey" as its focus, with no bourbon mentioned. Core range presumed unpeated; catalogue also lists "Boulder Peated Malt" as a distinct expression -- likely already caught by the central "peated" keyword rule, no producer rule added. defaultTypeName left empty since it is unclear whether the whole range is single malt only.

Single generic product line with no other qualifier; "Boulevardier" is otherwise a classic bourbon/Campari/vermouth cocktail name, so this may be a bottled RTD cocktail mis-filed under whisky rather than an actual whiskey brand (same concern as Ice Drive, see final report) rather than a whiskey brand -- left fully unknown.

Bouteille is simply French for "bottle" -- this may be a scraping/page-structure artifact (a label word mistaken for the brand) rather than a genuine brand name; flagged for human review rather than skipped outright, since it is plausibly real French whisky with an unidentifiable brand string. No producer found this session either way.
Peated to ~25-30 ppm phenol, mid-range on Islay

Bradan Orach is Speyburn's entry-level NAS single malt; catalogue lists it under this name rather than 'Speyburn'. Peat inferred from the parent distillery's standard unpeated Speyside profile, not a Bradan-Orach-specific citation, hence confidence=low.

Historically named "Braes of Glenlivet" (the catalogue's spelling, and still used by independent bottlers, e.g. Douglas Laing per sample); renamed Braeval in the 1990s. Standard unpeated Speyside malt.

Colorado craft distillery, confirmed via Wikipedia as a cask supplier to Kilchoman and an award-winning aquavit producer; bourbon-based range (Blend, Rum/PX/Port cask finishes, Distiller's High Proof). No peat indication found; American whiskey is not traditionally peat-kilned per cited page.

French single malt, distilled in Cognac from estate-grown heirloom barley (founder Allison Parc). Official site markets it as smooth and approachable but states no peat/smoke information either way, so left unknown rather than assumed.

Wikipedia: produced heavily peated whisky 1969-1973 (covering an Islay/Caol Ila shortfall), with most whisky made under the Brora name after 1973 in a 'lightly peated Highland style' before closure in 1983; reopened 2021 (still very young stock, no core range profile confirmed yet). scotchwhisky.com's whiskypedia entry: 'you will find Broras which are immensely oily and smoky, as well as some in which there is the merest exhalation of peat' -- i.e. genuinely variable by vintage. Classified medium as a defensible midpoint; a reviewer should treat individual releases as ranging from light to heavy.

Added because Port Charlotte (this batch) references it via parentSlug. Core Bruichladdich-branded range is unpeated; siblings Port Charlotte (heavy) and Octomore (extreme, not in this batch) are separate producer rows
Standard Diageo blended Scotch since 1884; no peat or smoke character mentioned in sourced material.

Bud Spencer (samples: The Legend, The Legend Mini) most likely trades on the name of the Italian actor Carlo Pedersoli (stage name Bud Spencer) as licensed merchandise; Wikipedia search only returns his biography, no dedicated drinks-brand page. Could not confirm whether the liquid is actually whisky (celebrity-branded rum is at least as plausible) -- flagging for reviewer attention rather than guessing kind/country/peat.
Standard Kentucky straight bourbon, unpeated.
Bourbon (Shelbyville/Lebanon KY) and rye (Lawrenceburg IN) come from two different mashbills/sites, so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat/smoke mentioned

Wikipedia: "one of the milder single malt Islay whiskies"; the Islay article groups it with Bowmore/Bruichladdich/Caol Ila as "substantially lighter in taste" than Laphroaig/Ardbeg. Core range unpeated; its Mòine range is heavily peated (see rule.tsv) per the research brief's own worked example — that specific pairing was not independently re-verified via an opened source.

No Wikipedia article. Guessed official domains for 'Deeside Brewery & Distillery' either failed TLS validation or resolved to an unrelated parked-domain sales page; the real site was not located this session. Nothing fetchable to cite.

Well-documented teaspoon name Cadenhead uses for undisclosed Balvenie (per this project's research brief). Peat inferred from parent Balvenie's core unpeated range since no source names Burnside specifically; short/generic English word so alias scope is brand not any.

Distillery is in Bushmills, County Antrim, Northern Ireland (UK, not the Republic of Ireland) -- GB used since no GB-NIR code exists in the closed list. Range spans single malt (10/12/16/21yo) and blended (Original, Black Bush, Red Bush) so defaultTypeName left empty. Irish whiskey wiki page: peat is rarely used outside Scotland, no exception listed for Bushmills. Country normalized GB -> IE: the closed list has no GB-NIR and this seed follows the Irish-whiskey GI convention.

Wikipedia confirms Diageo ownership and Speyside/Dufftown location. No Mortlach-specific peat statement found; peat=none inferred from Speyside's general unpeated house style (cited page states peat use is uncommon there), not from a Mortlach-specific source, so confidence kept low.

Independent bottler of classic Independent Bottler Malts since 2017; also owns Torabhaig (peated, Skye) and Reivers (grain) distilleries. Vintage Casks samples name Glen Spey, Dufftown and Mannochmore; distillery rows added for each below.
Not researched (budget); "Moulin" is ambiguous (French for "mill"; also a place name in Highland Scotland), so countryCode left empty rather than guessed.
Historic-sounding Scotch blend name; no citation found this session (Wikipedia search returned nothing on point).

Confirmed independent bottler of vintage single malts, grains and blended malts. Distillery rows added below for Mortlach/Macallan/Bunnahabhain/Caol Ila/Bowmore/Laphroaig/North British, all named in this brand's samples.

Japanese Muteki sample claims Japanese origin, but true origin was not verified this pass (some "Japanese-style" whiskies are blended/bottled outside Japan); countryCode left as XX (unspecified) and peat unknown rather than assumed.

Sherry-cask blended malt from The Macallan, Highland Park, Glenturret and Glenrothes; rebranded 'Naked Malt' in 2018. One constituent (Highland Park) is medium-peated, but the finished blend's own tasting notes describe rich/fruity sherry character with no smoke, so recorded as none. Ownership was Edrington; ownership of the sibling Famous Grouse brand moved to William Grant & Sons in 2024/2025 (see famous-grouse) -- left owner empty here since Naked Malt's own sale was not separately confirmed.

Organic distillery at Drimnin on the Morvern peninsula (mainland Highland, opposite Mull); founded by Annabel Thomas, independent - owner left empty. Catalogue brand string 'Nc Nean' (no apostrophe) aliased here
Could not identify this brand within budget (possibly a small/regional producer); left entirely unknown.
Nashville, TN revival distillery (Nelson's Green Brier Distillery); Tennessee whiskey is a corn-based, charcoal-mellowed style unrelated to peat. Not independently re-verified this pass.

Independent craft distillery in Newport, Kentucky, confirmed real via the Kentucky Bourbon Trail wiki page ("Northern Craft Tour: New Riff Distillery in Newport"). Produces both bourbon and rye (samples: Malted Rye, Bottled in Bond, Bottled-in-Bond Rye) so defaultTypeName left empty. Bourbon/rye are not peated categories.

Samples are the Gold & Gold sub-range. Nikka's two malt distilleries differ (Yoichi peated, Miyagikyo unpeated) and the fetched Wikipedia article does not state Gold & Gold's blend composition, so left unknown rather than guessed.

Could not verify this brand this session (no Wikipedia page, no resolvable official site). Flagged for a human to check authenticity -- some Japanese-sounding export blends are not actually distilled in Japan.
Willett small-batch bourbon label, Bardstown, KY.

Smoke Symphony and "Orchard Outburst" - could not identify this brand this session (WebSearch budget exhausted, no working URL guessed). "Smoke Symphony" naming hints at a possible smoky/peated expression, which is exactly why it is left unknown rather than guessed - flagged for a human reviewer.
No information found within budget (no Wikipedia coverage). Origin and type undetermined.

Undisclosed-source single malt label per BRIEF.md's rule 3 (same pattern as "Secret Orkney"/"Speyside's Finest"), named after Edinburgh's historic (drained) Nor Loch. No web presence found this session; not guessing the source distillery.

Grain distillery, Edinburgh, founded 1885. Region left empty (grain, no malt-region classification) but legalRegion set to lowland since it is physically in Edinburgh. Referenced only as a component of a Murray McDavid vatting ("Air Leth").

No dedicated Wikipedia article; two guessed official domains (northpointdistillery.com, northpointdistillers.com) both answered 200 but rendered no readable text on a plain fetch (JS-heavy site), so no citable content was found either way.

Official site confirms its whisky ('Uist Whisky') is 'soon to launch' as of this research, with a 2026 founders-club cask scheme still selling - no released/characterized spirit yet. Their existing product line is the 'Downpour' gin range (a different brand name, gin only, out of scope here).
No web presence found this session; apostrophe-surname styling suggests an Irish-themed own-label, unconfirmed.
No web presence found this session; Irish-surname styling suggests an Irish whiskey own-label, unconfirmed.
Presumed Irish whiskey brand by name; could not find a dedicated source this session. Peat=none per general Irish-whiskey category norm, confidence low.
No dedicated source found. Irish-surname branding with cask-finished Rum/Port/Sherry variants strongly suggests an own-label Irish blend. Peat via the Irish-whiskey category source.
No information found for this brand within budget (Wikipedia search returned only unrelated people/topics named Oakeshott). Origin and type unknown.

Mainland west-coast Argyll town, not one of the market-convention "islands" -- region=highland matches the authority TSV. Wiki: whisky described as "West Highland" flavour "falling between the dry, smoky style of the...islands and the lighter, sweeter malts of the Highlands", i.e. lightly smoky.
Super-heavily peated - described as the most heavily peated whisky in the world (100-300+ ppm). Named directly in this batch's Bruichladdich sample products ("Octomore 13.3").

Two catalogue entries share this stem with different invented-sounding regional flourishes ("Highland Phantom Peak", "Speyside Celestia Creek"); no web presence found for either. Likely an own-label range with a region-themed name per bottling, but the specific distillery/region cannot be confirmed, so region is left empty rather than picked arbitrarily; kept as one producer row covering both catalogue entries.

O.H. Ingram River Aged/"...Flagship" -- initials-plus-surname is a common American whiskey brand-naming convention (cf. E.H. Taylor, W.L. Weller), so US is a low-confidence inference from the name alone; no citation confirms the specific producer. Peat citation is the general non-Scotch-unpeated statement (see canadian-club note).
No web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per budget policy.

Tomintoul distillery's peated single malt, released under its old spring-name "Ballantruan" rather than the Tomintoul brand name. Wiki: "a 1991 peaty vintage was released under the name 'Old Ballantruan'"..."it has released a peated single malt called Ballantruan". No phenol ppm figure found in the source; general reputation (and the fact it is marketed as Tomintoul's peat-forward counterpart) supports heavy over medium, but the exact figure is not confirmed -- confidence kept low rather than high.

No web presence found. Catalogue calls it "bourbon" but it is sold from Spain, an unusual combination -- left type/peat unknown rather than trust the bourbon guess. Similar unidentifiable own-label pattern to the existing "Jim Bardett" row from another batch (different spelling; not assumed to be the same producer).
No source found (single-product own label); treated as ordinary blended Scotch per category convention.
Generic name, no identifiable web presence found; single-product own label.

Revived historic Irish whiskey brand (original Comber Distillery, County Down, closed 1956); current "Old Comber" (2021 release) is pot still whiskey matured in bourbon/sherry/ruby port casks by Echlinville Distillery, which took over the brand. No peat mentioned; Irish pot still whiskey is standardly unpeated.
Historic low-priced Kentucky straight bourbon brand, distilled by Suntory Global Spirits (Beam Suntory) alongside Jim Beam (confirmed via Wikipedia search result text). Standard bourbon, no peat.

Ezra Brooks-family line bottled by Lux Row Distillers (see lux-row row in this file). Samples span both rye ('Rye Full Proof') and bourbon ('7 Bourbon Barrel Strength'), so defaultTypeName left empty. American whiskey category default applied for peat.
Kentucky straight bourbon, continuously on the market since 1870; now has its own dedicated distillery on Louisville's Whiskey Row.
No web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per budget policy.

Hunter Laing & Co's flagship single-cask range, spanning many distilleries (Wikipedia confirms the 2013 Douglas Laing/Hunter Laing split; Hunter Laing's own Scarabus listing confirms the company bottles single malt independently). Modeled as kind=bottler since the range spans many distilleries with no single house peat level. Scarabus (separate row) is also a Hunter Laing product; bottlerSlug=old-malt-cask stands in for the parent company to avoid inventing an extra 'hunter-laing' row.

One of the oldest continuously produced American whiskey brands (since 1810), produced at Jim Beam's distillery. 'jim-beam' is a well-known distillery slug another batch will almost certainly emit -- not created here.

Blended malt Scotch brand; owner not verified this session (commonly attributed to Morrison Scotch Whisky Distillers but unconfirmed here). No indication of peat in samples (Original/Cask Strength/Double Sherry Wood).
Marketed as 'The Genuine Maritime Malt'; unpeated.

Hunter Laing's "Old & Rare Platinum Selection" single-cask range; each release names its source distillery. Distillery rows added for the samples: Arran, Dufftown, Glenturret, Bunnahabhain, Glen Garioch, Highland Park. Parent company "Hunter Laing" itself is not emitted as its own row here; another batch may.

Van Winkle family's wheated-bourbon brand, distilled/bottled by Sazerac at Buffalo Trace under a joint venture since 2002. No explicit peat statement found (sources covered ownership/history, not tasting notes); inferred unpeated from standard bourbon mashbill

Single-barrel cask-strength Kentucky straight bourbon bottled by Augusta Distillery (Augusta, KY), the distillery's inaugural bourbon. Sourced from an undisclosed Kentucky distillery ('rumored' Heaven Hill, not confirmed) so no parentSlug given per the undisclosed-origin rule. No smoke/peat in tasting notes (oak-char notes only).
Not researched (budget); generic "Old ___'s" own-label naming, origin unconfirmed.
Campari Group acquired Old Smuggler (with Glen Grant and Braemar) from Pernod Ricard in 2006; standard blended Scotch, no peat indication.

Blended Scotch (min. 25% malt content) evoking the historic Tullymet distillery (built 1812 as Auchnagie, renamed Tullymet 1890, long since closed) -- heritage branding, not a claim that the liquid comes from that site. No peat/smoke mentioned; described as smooth and elegant.
Kentucky Straight Bourbon, La Martiniquaise portfolio (sourced, not own distillery). No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated - standard bourbon mashbill, no peated malt mentioned
Single product, no information found this session, not searched (long tail budget)

Marketed as "Japanese blended whisky" ("Oni" demon + "Kishi" knight); brand page describes cedar/lightly-smoked malt notes alongside dominant floral and honey character in both expressions (Demon Knight, Deadly Sakura) — not marketed as a peated whisky. Milestone Beverages may be a distributor/marketing brand owner rather than the actual distiller.
Catalogue supplied no type/country guess; no web presence found. Own-label, origin unclear -- possibly an invented Irish-sounding name rather than genuinely Irish.

IMPORTANT correction to this task's framing: Orkney Distilling Ltd's flagship 'Kirkjuvagr' name is GIN ONLY (confirmed via the official site's own product navigation: 'Kirkjuvagr Gin', 'Special Edition Gin') - it is NOT their whisky brand. Their actual whisky is sold as 'Fara' and 'Rysa' (both labelled Blended Malt Scotch Whisky, i.e. vatted from multiple distilleries' malt, not a single-distillery malt of their own), added below as separate kind=blend rows with real peat citations from the same official site. This distillery-level row is left peatProfile=unknown since the range spans both an unpeated line (Fara) and a lightly-peated one (Rysa) - never averaged, per this task's own sibling-brand rule. Collision safety: the catalogue's 'An Orkney'/'Cask Orkney'/"Probably Orkney's Finest" are Highland Park or undisclosed, NOT this company - alias kept brand-scope.

Diageo's rare/sourced-whiskey project releasing single malts and bourbons from various (including mothballed) distilleries under many release names (Rhetoric, Barterhouse, Old Blowhard, Muckety-Muck, Woven Honor...). Bottler-style range, no single house peat level.

Rhetoric is an aged-bourbon release under the Orphan Barrel project; the specific source distillery/mashbill for this release was not confirmed this session so kept as kind=blend rather than naming a distillery. Standard bourbon category, no peat.
Brand sold by Irish Distillers/Pernod Ricard to Sazerac in 2016; production continues under contract at Midleton. No explicit peat statement found; inferred from standard Irish blend convention

Heaven Hill's annual limited-edition bourbon/rye/wheat series named for Parker Beam. defaultTypeName left empty since editions vary by grain/type year to year; all are American whiskey, hence unpeated.
Confirmed blend of Highland and Lowland malts, historically made at Seagram's Speyside distilleries, now owned by Chivas Brothers/Pernod Ricard; introduced 1965. No Islay/peated component described.

Goa, India. Flagship "Brilliance" is unpeated. "Edited" is mildly peated; "Bold" and Select Cask "Peated" use peat carried to Goa from Islay (Bold measured about 25ppm) -- see rules. The "none" here reflects the flagship/default expression, not the whole range.

Pearse Lyons Distillery, Dublin (former St James' Church), opened 2017, founded by Dr Pearse Lyons. Range includes a blend ('Pearse Distillers Blend') alongside single malt/pot still releases, so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat mentioned; Irish whiskey of this style is typically unpeated.

Widely known in general whisky knowledge as a Wemyss Malts blended malt named for its peat character, but every citable source attempted this session (Wemyss's own site, The Whisky Exchange, distiller.com, whisky.com) returned a connection failure or 403. Left peatProfile unknown per the no-citation rule despite the suggestive name -- flagging as a likely "heavy" for reviewer confirmation.

Created by Eamonn Jones and Gerald Erdrich; consistently marketed/reviewed as an intensely, heavily peated Islay-style whisky. Source distillery is not disclosed (one source notes peat is also used outside Islay), so no parentSlug is set even though retail listings brand it "Islay"; defaultTypeName left empty since sourcing/type description is inconsistent (single malt vs multi-distillery).
Core Madeira/Sherrywood/Portwood expressions are unpeated. A distinct Peated expression (and the Dragon range's 'Celt') exists, see rule.tsv.

New Jersey-based bourbon brand (per List of wineries, breweries, and distilleries in New Jersey search result); non-distiller producer blending sourced bourbon (Four Grain, Architect, cask finishes). Peat-kilning is specifically a Scotch practice per cited page; no US bourbon peat indication found.
No web presence found. Unlike most of this batch's unidentified own labels, the name has no 'Glen'/Scottish styling, so it was left unclassified rather than defaulted to blended Scotch.
Brand not independently verified via any source actually opened (no hits found); American-themed name suggests US whiskey, category default (peat is a Scotch-specific practice) applied.

Originally created by Spencerfield Spirit Company; acquired by Ian Macleod Distillers with their purchase of Spencerfield Spirits in September 2016 (confirmed via Wikipedia). Listed among Ian Macleod's core blended-Scotch brands, explicitly contrasted there with their peated Smokehead single malt -- read as implicitly unpeated.
Canadian whisky brand, confirmed as a Corby Spirit and Wine product (rum/bourbon-barrel finished). No peat tradition in Canadian whisky.
Straight rye whiskey brand of Heaven Hill Distillery, confirmed via a Wikipedia search snippet listing Heaven Hill's rye brands as Pikesville and Rittenhouse.
Redwood Empire's "Pipe Dream Bourbon Whiskey" (confirmed via their own site). Standard American whiskey, no peat.

Platte Valley 100% Straight Corn Whiskey, McCormick Distilling Company, Weston, Missouri (catalogue spells the brand Platte Walley). Corn whiskey is not in the closed defaultTypeName list so left empty.

Small-batch New Zealand single malt distillery in the Waikato region (near the Bombay Hills). Official site's homepage and 'Our Whisky' page state no peat/smoke information for any expression (Ringbearer, Core Range, Exploration Series, Single Casks) -- left unknown rather than guessed.

Jacopo Poli is a well-known Italian grappa/brandy house (Bassano del Grappa, Veneto); could not confirm this session whether "Segretario di Stato" is genuinely a whisky release of theirs or a mislabeled grappa/brandy product (poligrappa.com returned 404 / redirected to an Italian-only page with no whisky content found). Kept as a low/unknown-confidence row rather than skipped outright, since the catalogue explicitly classifies it "malt"/IT -- flagged for human review of whether this is whisky at all.

Curated range of undisclosed single malts from various Islay distilleries (Elixir Distillers keeps sources confidential; enthusiasts widely link some batches to Caol Ila/Laphroaig/Bunnahabhain, none officially confirmed). Every release is marketed around Islay's 'smoky, maritime character', so peat is recorded as heavy despite the source distillery being left blank per the undisclosed-label rule.
Bruichladdich's heavily peated brand, ~40ppm

Diageo's own site (malts.com) describes it as having an 'elegant, peated coastal character' and calls the whisky 'prized for its rarity and refined peated character' - confirms peated but not an exact intensity. Classed 'heavy' rather than 'medium' on well-established historical consensus grouping it with Lagavulin/Caol Ila (same regional maltings/era) rather than Highland Park/Bowmore's medium tier - a reviewer may want a source with an explicit ppm figure. Closed 1983, reopened 2024; one of the most sought-after 'ghost distilleries' among independent bottlers for decades.

UK's first vertical distillery (Edinburgh; opened to the public Oct 2023, but new-make production only began early 2024) - under the 3-year minimum, so no legal Scotch has been released yet to characterize.

Historic Irish whiskey brand (Dublin, est. 1791), now produced at Midleton; range spans blended and single pot still, so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat mentioned; Irish whiskey is standardly unpeated.

Historic Powers brand's flagship pot-still expression, distilled at Midleton. 'midleton' is a well-known Irish distillery slug that another batch will very likely emit (home of Jameson/Redbreast/Midleton Very Rare) -- not created in this file to avoid a low-value duplicate. Category default applied for peat.

Single product 'Ley Seca' (Spanish for 'dry law' / Prohibition). No whiskey/whisky brand by this name found on Wikipedia; 'Ley Seca' itself only returns the generic Prohibition term and an unrelated song. Left fully unknown -- flag for human review of what this product actually is (category/country not even confirmed).

No web presence found (no Wikipedia page, no resolvable official site) despite three samples in this batch (Bourbon Casks, Peated Small Batch No.2, Selected Casks) suggesting a small/single-cask-style range. See rule.tsv for the "Peated" exception, evidenced directly by the product's own name rather than an external source.

Blend of triple-distilled malt and grain whiskey, founded by Conor McGregor (Eire Born Spirits), now majority-owned by Proximo Spirits. No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated from Irish tradition and tasting notes (vanilla, honey, toasted wood) with no smoke mentioned

The distillery's own name is 'Pulteney' (est. 1826, Wick); 100% of its retail output is marketed as 'Old Pulteney'. An existing out/02/producer.tsv row already covers slug=old-pulteney (kind=distillery, no parentSlug, peatProfile=none/high) - this row is added alongside it so an independent bottler's cask labelled the bare distillery name 'Pulteney' (without 'Old') still resolves, exactly the Gordon & MacPhail Ledaig-style pattern this whole task targets. ARCHITECTURE NOTE for a human reviewer: ideally old-pulteney would carry kind=brand + parentSlug=pulteney to match the intended distillery/brand split (see this task's own worked example for Pulteney/Old Pulteney) - I have not edited that file, only flagged it here. Wikipedia: marketed 'The Genuine Maritime Malt', character attributed to sea-air exposure during maturation; no peat mentioned anywhere in the article.

Italian single malt distillery, Glurns, Venosta Valley, South Tyrol. Official site's current range (Core/ARTE/AURA/CUBO) shows no peated expression; combined with the general category fact that peat is rare outside Scotland.
~12yo small-batch bourbon, part of Willett's Small Batch Boutique Bourbon Collection.

Heaven Hill Quality House Old Style White appears to be a bottling/export label of Heaven Hill's Old Style White product. defaultTypeName left empty (mashbill/style of "Old Style White" unclear from samples). Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.

Produced by Niche Drinks in Derry (first Irish whiskey bottled there in over 100 years) for Luxco, a US company now owned by MGP Ingredients. Range spans a blend and an 8-year-old single malt, so defaultTypeName left empty. Derry is technically in Northern Ireland (UK) but the product is marketed under the "Irish whiskey" geographic category, so countryCode is set to IE consistent with that convention. No source found confirming peat status, left unknown rather than assumed. Catalogue brand string for this row is "Luxco".

Official site: the flagship single malt is 'Lightly peated and balanced with rich, dark fruit flavours' - a deliberate house style combining peated and unpeated new-make. First legal whisky released Sept 2020; the earlier 'While We Wait' releases (2017-2020) were independently-bottled previews, not the distillery's own matured spirit.

Louisville, KY distillery; Core Four line (Cavehill, Heigold, Dareringer, Boxergrail) spans bourbon and a 95%-rye whiskey (Boxergrail), so defaultTypeName left empty. Official site describes mashbills with no peated malt; American whiskey mash bills do not use peat, but no source explicitly states "unpeated", hence confidence=low.

Not researched (budget). "Ragtime" + "Rye" is a strongly American-coded name; countryCode/defaultTypeName inferred from the name only. Peat left unknown per no-citation policy (American rye is conventionally unpeated but this was not verified for this specific brand).
Irish whiskey (triple-distilled grain + double-distilled malt blend), aged 10 years in ex-bourbon casks, bottled for the German band Rammstein. No peat reported (standard Irish blend style).

Renamed from "Rebel Yell" in 2020 (catalogue lists both names, both aliased here to one row); distilled at Lux Row Distillers, Bardstown KY. No source explicitly states unpeated - inferred from standard bourbon mashbill with no peated-malt mention
Distilled at Midleton. The Irish whiskey article confirms peat is rare outside Scotland and lists Redbreast among the standard (non-peated) single pot still whiskeys.

Northern California craft whiskey producer. Official site (fetched this session) confirms "Emerald Giant" as a rye whiskey; range also spans bourbon and a "Foggy Burl Single Malt", so defaultTypeName is left empty. No peat/smoke mentioned anywhere on the fetched page; rye/bourbon mashbills do not use peated malt by convention.

Mossburn's own site contrasts its two distilleries directly: 'Torabhaig and Reivers are poles apart, sitting at opposite ends of the whisky-making spectrum' - Torabhaig makes 'an extremely characterful, peated new-make spirit', so Reivers (first Single Grain Scotch Whisky planned for 2020, Scottish Borders) is positioned as its unpeated opposite. Note: this URL currently returns HTTP 404 despite serving this real page content (a site-routing quirk on their end) - a human reviewer may want to re-check it lands correctly.
Part of the unresolved Japanese-styled budget cluster (see Shinobu); single product, no web presence found this session

MGP Ingredients brand (Wikipedia's List of whisky brands: George Remus Bourbon, MGP Ingredients, Lawrenceburg, Indiana). Range spans bourbon and rye (Remus Highest Rye sample), so defaultTypeName left empty.

Richmond, Virginia craft distillery; official site lists bourbon, rye and corn whiskey with no peat mention. defaultTypeName left empty since range spans multiple types. Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.

Independent bottler/whisky broker, named after the Argyll mountain pass; no dedicated citation found this session (Wikipedia and Bing searches returned nothing on point), general trade-knowledge identification only, hence low confidence even on category. Samples name two REAL distilleries (Benrinnes, Bruichladdich -- rows emitted below, per authority file) plus 'Strathenry' and 'Finglassie', which do NOT appear in the Wikipedia Scottish-distilleries authority list (259 rows) -- treated as invented/undisclosed single-cask names per the brief's undisclosed-label rule, no distillery row created for them and no guess made at the true source.

No country stated by the catalogue and no producer identified this session. defaultTypeName=rye taken from the catalogue's own guess; peatProfile=none rests on the general rye-whiskey-is-unpeated category convention (peated malt is not used in American rye mashbills), not a brand-specific source.
Bottled-in-Bond 100 proof rye, mashbill 51% rye / 37% corn / 12% malted barley. Historic Pennsylvania rye brand; Heaven Hill bought it in 1993.

Could not identify this brand (WebSearch budget exhausted, no working URL found via WebFetch). All 3 sample names are just "River Proof Series" with no other descriptor - flagged for a human reviewer with search access; "Proof" naming hints at American whiskey but this is a guess, not asserted in any field.
Catalogue supplied no type/country guess; no web presence found. Own-label, origin unclear.
Tribute blend licensed by the World Federation of Robert Burns Clubs, produced by Isle of Arran Distillers; treated as an ordinary unpeated blended Scotch, not independently re-verified this pass.

Blended malt combining single malts from Islay, Arran, Jura and Orkney (formerly "Rock Oyster"). Source confirms the composition but does not describe smoke/peat intensity; since only one of the four source islands (Islay) is reliably peated and the others are unpeated/lightly peated, "light" is a conservative estimate, not a confirmed figure - kept low confidence, flagged for a reviewer.

Catalogue spells the brand 'Roe + Co'; official/Wikipedia spelling is 'Roe & Co'. Distillery established 2019 in Dublin (Thomas Street), owned by Diageo; flagship product is a Blended Irish whiskey. No peat/smoke mentioned.

Classic triple-distilled Lowland malt, historically dubbed 'King of the Lowlands'; Wikipedia describes its character as fruits, grasses and flowers, with no peat mention anywhere in the article. Closed 1993 (original stills stolen 2008/09), trademark and site acquired by Ian Macleod Distillers in 2017, rebuilt and reopened 2023. One of the most famous 'ghost distilleries' among independent bottlers for the decades it was closed.

Built mainly to supply Diageo's blends; occasional single malt Special Releases since September 2023, and malt from here was used in Johnnie Walker Black Ruby (2024/2025). No peat information found -- large Diageo blending distilleries often run more than one peat level, so unpeated should not be assumed.
MGP Ingredients' first proprietary rye label (launched 2018), produced at their Lawrenceburg, Indiana distillery.
Willett Distillery's best-selling brand (wiki: "Rowan's Creek bourbon (50.05% abv, No age statement) -- This is Willett Distillery's best-selling brand"). Bourbon is not a peated category.
Same Highland regional-character basis as Dalmore/Glencadam/Macduff.
Brand not independently confirmed beyond the category (no hits found); Canadian whisky category default (conventionally a blend, conventionally unpeated) applied.
Ultra-premium blended Scotch launched 1953, blended/matured at Strathisla. The standard/Signature range is not peated; a distinct "21 Year Old The Peated Blend" exists, see rule.

Catalogue brand string for this row is "Seagram's Gin" but the sample product is "Seagram's Royal Stag Deluxe" - an Indian whisky (blend of grain spirits + imported Scotch malts), not a gin; almost certainly a shop miscategorisation. Row created for the actual (whisky) product; exact "Seagram's Gin" catalogue string aliased here - FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW. No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated

Vertically integrated single malt distillery in Rozelieures, Lorraine (own barley, malting, distilling, maturation); founded early 2000s, first release 2007. Base/Origine range unpeated -- see rule.tsv for the separate Tourbe (peated) line.
Samples ('Ruediger', 'Oloroso Sherry Cask') read as a German-market brand but this is unconfirmed; two fetch attempts this session failed (403/404)

Catalogue samples (Cigar Series, Cask Strength, Madeira Cask Strength) suggest a small craft/private rye-style label. No Wikipedia page or other citable source found this session; country and category undetermined.

Orkney Distilling Ltd's peated Blended Malt Scotch Whisky, named for the uninhabited Orkney island of Rysa. Official site: 'Gentle peat smoke meets rich dried fruit and creme brulee sweetness, with hints of burnt leather and pepper' - a gentle/light peat, not a heavy one.
No web presence found; own-label, origin unclear. Catalogue's own country guess was blank.

column7: Sakurao Brewery and Distillery Co., Ltd
column15: Hiroshima Prefecture distillery, distillation started October 2018; range includes gin as well as whisky, peat level not confirmed this session.

Believed to be a Kentucky Straight Bourbon private label commonly sold in European discount retail (general market knowledge), but no dedicated source was found/opened this session, so defaultTypeName is left empty rather than asserted as bourbon. Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.

Historic Northern Irish whiskey brand (associated with Henry Neill, Rockport House, Co. Down); today mainly visible as the sponsorship name of the Irish Cup football competition. Current producer/owner unconfirmed. countryCode set to GB since Northern Ireland has no dedicated code in the closed list (GB-ENG/SCT/WLS don't apply, and IE is the Republic of Ireland). Peat via the Irish-whiskey category source (peat rare outside Scotland). Country normalized GB -> IE: the closed list has no GB-NIR and this seed follows the Irish-whiskey GI convention.

Consumer spirits brand co-founded by actor Sam Heughan (Outlander) and Alex Norouzi in 2021; Sassenach gin was contract-distilled at the Newton Stewart site since renamed Galloway Distillery (formerly Crafty distillery), and Wikipedia reports (Nov 2025) that Sassenach whisky and vodka production was being 'brought in-house' there too.
